question.text: After Nicholas abdicated, he and his family were executed, paving the way for this Bolshevik ("BOWL-she-vick") leader to assume power.
question.clue: This politician attacked social democrats in his April Theses, and returned to Russia in a "sealed train" to oppose the Mensheviks.

swap.text: This first tsar of Russia led the unsuccessful Livonian War. He was known for his cruelty, which could be seen in his killing of his second son.
swap.answerHtml: Ivan the Terrible [or Ivan IV of Russia; or Ivan Vasilyevich; or Ivan Grozny; prompt on Ivan]
swap.clue: He created a secret police called the Oprichniki and he created the first "assembly of the land," the Zemskii Sobor.

question.leadin: He fought in the Great Northern War and created the Table of Ranks.
question.text: This is what Russian czar who cut off the beards of the boyars in an attempt to westernize Russia?
question.answerHtml: Peter the Great [or Peter I; or Pyotr Velikiy; prompt on Peter]
question.clue: This monarch's half-sister Sophia was forced to become a nun after the streltsy, whom this monarch disbanded, revolted on her behalf.

swap.text: This leader's policies, including glasnost and perestroika, led to the end of the Soviet Union. He was famously implored by Reagan to tear down the Berlin Wall.
swap.clue: This successor to Konstantin Chernenko removed troops from Afghanistan and instituted liberal policies such as the "restructuring" Perestroika.

question.leadin: The nurse Darya Mikhailova ("mih-HAIL-oh-vuh") took care of Russian soldiers from this war wounded at the Battle of Alma.
question.text: Name this 1853-1856 war, during which Sevastopol ("seh-VAST-oh-pull") was besieged for eleven months. A group of 38 nurses worked at the Scutari Barracks during this war.
question.clue: During this war the French victory at the Battle of Malakoff ended the Siege of Sevastopol, and miscommunication between Lord Raglan and Lord Cardigan caused the Charge of the Light Brigade at the Battle of Balaclava.

swap.leadin: After bragging about this city's riches, the Tartars allegedly hooked Nikita Shchemyaka ["sh-chim-yah-kah"] by the tongue to his horse's tail, saying that it will take him there.
swap.text: Name this city, which was the capital of the Rus ["roos"] state until it was sacked by Batu Khan. This modern-day city is the capital of Ukraine.
swap.clue: A ruler of this city militarily supported the Byzantine emperor Basil II, which resulted in the formation of the Varangian Guard, in exchange for marrying Basil II's sister Anna.

question.leadin: During this conflict, the Green armies were formed by peasants to prevent other belligerents from requisitioning supplies from their villages.
question.text: Name this conflict in which one side utilized "war communism" to defeat the White Army. That victorious side also briefly allied with and later attacked the Black Army of anarchist Nestor Makhno during this conflict.
question.clue: "War communism" was implemented by the winners of this conflict to ensure supplies for its army.

swap.leadin: Name some things about the dissolution of the Soviet Union.
swap.text: This man was the last head of state of the Soviet Union, serving from 1988 until its dissolution in 1991.
swap.clue: The GKChP attempted to remove this man from power during the failed August Coup of 1991.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the Greek historian Xenophon.
question.text: According to Xenophon, the Ten Thousand cried "Thalatta! Thalatta!" after seeing this sea near the city of Trebizond, meaning they had returned to Greek city-states.
question.clue: To defend one of its ports, Eduard Totleben ordered a fleet sunk to block the harbor, and the subsequent siege ended after the taking of Malakoff Redoubt.

swap.text: The G7 became the G8 when, despite its weak economy, this country was added for political reasons. For calendar year 2006, its president occupies the chair of the G8.
swap.clue: The mostly-defunct political party Yabloko is a protest voice in this country.

question.leadin: This man conducted an impromptu debate with President Nixon in 1959 in an American model kitchen.
question.text: Name this Soviet premier, who denounced Stalin's cult of personality in the "Secret Speech."
question.clue: On a trip to the United States, this man met Iowa farmer Roswell Garst and he attempted to raise the USSR's agricultural output by initiating the Virgin Lands Campaign in Kazakhstan.

swap.leadin: This program's most expensive project was an attempt to create the "Buran."
swap.text: Identify this broad program which enjoyed great success with the Vostok missions in the early 1960s and was formally ended in 1991. We are looking for the program, not any specific agency.
swap.answerHtml: Soviet space program [accept obvious description, do not accept “Russian space program”]
swap.clue: The largest conventional detonation at the time occurred during a test of the N1 for this program.

question.text: From the 2000s onwards, this leader oversaw construction of the Astravets Nuclear Power Plant. Protestors targeted this long-serving leader in the Jeans Revolution.
question.answerHtml: Alexander Lukashenko [or Alexander Grigoryevich Lukashenko; or Alyaksandr Ryhoravich Lukashenka] (Alexander Lukashenko is the president of Belarus.)
question.clue: During a 2006 press conference, this man claimed that he rigged the vote to lower his own totals, since it is not a European outcome.

swap.text: Although he lost several initial battles at sites like Narva, this Russian leader quickly reorganized his army and proceeded to go on to win at Poltava and the Pruth River.
swap.answer: Peter I or Peter the Great
swap.clue: This ruler tortured a son named Alexei who died in jail.

question.leadin: This ruler came to power in a coup that overthrew the successors of Anna.
question.text: Name this Russian ruler who put Ivan VI into prison. This ruler had earlier been banished from the court of Peter II due to the influence of the Dolgorukovs.
question.clue: This ruler removed the tongue of Natalia Lopukhina, as part of a longtime grudge against the Mons family, after a failed intrigue aimed at toppling chancellor Alexey Bestuzhev.

swap.leadin: One of these men who was assassinated was likely Grigory Otrepyev, and another one of these men established his base in Tushino.
swap.text: Name these men, the last of whom was possibly named Sidorka and the first of whom came to power in 1605.
swap.clue: The first of these people was alleged to be a defrocked monk named Grigory Otrepiev by a Mussorgsky opera in which he was the main villain.

question.text: After the death of Feodor III, the Miloslavsky family incited this group of guardsmen to riot against the Naryshkins and other political leaders. One of their leaders was Ivan Khovansky.
question.clue: This group, which was initially armed with arquebuses, fought in the Siege of Kazan.

swap.text: This Russian tsar demanded that the Livonian confederation pay high taxes and occupied Dorpat and Narva, setting off the Livonian war.
swap.answer: Ivan IV or Ivan the Terrible
swap.clue: This son of Basil III prosecuted the Livonian War and suppressed Novgorod. Ruling from 1547 to 1584, this Rurikid was notable for maintaining the oprichina, a secret police force, and being an all-around mean dude.

question.leadin: This president lost popularity after censoring media coverage concerning his negotiations over the disputed Tuzla Island.
question.text: Give this president who pursued a dual policy of appeasing the West and Russia, known as his Multi-Vector Doctrine. This man's downfall ultimately occurred due his involvement in the assassination of journalistGeorgiy Gongadze.

swap.text: The Russians also had to form a special police unit to combat cannibalism during this battle. Despite enmity between Finland and Russia, Mannerheim refused to commit troops to this operation, which saw the Sinyavin Offensive and Operation Iskra.
